verses.1: And Ben-Saul heard that Abner had died in his tent. He broke his hands, and all of Israel became terrified.
verses.2: And there were two men who were priests. They were sons of Shaul. The name of one of them was Anah, and the name of the other was Rekab. They were descendants of Reimun from the tribe of Benyamin. For in those days, it was also considered important to be a descendant of Benyamin.
verses.3: And the Be’erotim fled during Githaima. They lived there until today.
verses.4: And Yehonatan, son of Shaul, son of Nekho, who was five years old at the time of Shaul’s death. Yehonatan came from Jerusalem. She carried him away, and in her haste, she fell and died. His name was Mefiboset.
verses.5: And the sons of Remon went in chariots and in horses. They arrived that day at the house of a man named Boas. He was the one who lay on the bed of those who were sick.
verses.6: And behold, they came to the inside of the house. They took the sheep and led them to the pen. Meanwhile, their brothers were taken away as prisoners.
verses.7: They entered the house. He lay on his bed in the courtyard. They covered him with a blanket, and he died. They took his head away from him. Then they went away along the road all night long.
verses.8: And they brought the head of the man who was beheaded to David, their friend. They said to the king, “Here is the head of the man who was beheaded, son of Saul. He sought your life. But Jehovah has given revenge on Saul and his descendants today.”
verses.9: And David repaired the chariot, and his brothers, the sons of Reimun the Beter. He said to them, “May the LORD live, who has saved my soul from all harm.”
verses.10: For the one who told me, he said, “Look! Shaul is dead.” And he acted as if he were seeing it with his own eyes. He grabbed him and killed him with a sword that I gave him.
verses.11: Even though those wicked people killed a righteous man in his own home, on his bed. Now I will seek his blood from your hands. And I will curse you from this earth.
verses.12: David ordered the boys to be killed. They were cut apart, with their hands and feet also severed. They were hung on the cross. The heads of those who died were taken away, and they were buried in the tomb in the city of Abner.
